subject: Intermittent control-plane connectivity during private VPC upgrade — postmortem and customer update
messages:
From: Alex Chu <alex.chu@nimbushealth.com>

Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@nimbushealth.com>
Date: 2025-11-18T09:17:00-08:00
Subject: API timeouts after scheduled update - Nimbus private VPC

Hi Marissa,

We started seeing intermittent 504/timeouts to the Redwood private endpoint for our private VPC around 08:45 PST, immediately after the scheduled minor control-plane upgrade you ran this morning. A subset (~18%) of requests intermittently fail with 504; others see large latency spikes (3–6x). This has affected our triage pipeline and some batch jobs.

Attached are a set of request traces and a short sampling of app logs. I also included a few trace IDs in case they’re helpful: trace-11-18-001, trace-11-18-017, trace-11-18-022.

Can you confirm whether this upgrade touched control-plane leader election or KV cache behavior for private deployments? We’re on a tight compliance window and need a short incident summary for our SRE review. Please advise next steps and ETA.

Thanks,
Alex Chu
Senior Infrastructure Engineer
Nimbus Health

[Attachment: control_plane_logs_20251118.zip (1.2MB)]

Subject: RE: API timeouts after scheduled update - Nimbus private VPC

Alex / Marissa — quick technical update from the triage team.

What we’ve observed so far:
- During the 08:30–09:00 rollout we briefly saw leader re-election events in the private control-plane cluster backing your tenancy; these coincided with elevated API latency and a subset of 504s.
- The upgrade included a minor control-plane scheduling/coordination change that toggles a new fast-fail path for stale KV entries. That toggle was incorrectly enabled for a small subset of private control-plane nodes due to a rollout rule mismatch.
- When the fast-fail path hit a node with a slightly different KV snapshot, it resulted in short-lived request failures and repeated retries that amplified latency.

Mitigations applied (11:00–11:20):
- Rolled back the scheduling toggle for the affected nodes and forced a KV resync.
- Applied a temporary routing rule so your product traffic prefers currently stable leader nodes.

Next steps:
- We’re continuing to validate stability across your endpoints; please run a short synthetic load (5–10 minutes) and share any failing traces.
- We will prepare an interim RCA and a full postmortem with timeline and remediation by 11/21.

Attachments: initial_kv_cache_snapshot.txt (trimmed)

Apologies for the disruption — we’ll keep this our top priority.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Principal Software Engineer, Platform
Redwood Inference

Subject: Interim incident summary and next steps — Nimbus private VPC (REL-2921)

Alex — following up with an interim summary while our postmortem is finalized. Thank you for your patience and for running the synthetic. High-level timeline and actions: 

Summary:
- Impact window: 2025-11-18 08:30–11:20 PST (elevated error rates and latency spikes following a scheduled control-plane minor upgrade).
- Scope: Affected a subset of requests routed through control-plane nodes with the misapplied fast-fail toggle (~18% of your traffic at peak).
- Immediate mitigations: rollback of toggle, KV resync, routing preference to stable leaders. Errors reduced after mitigations; residual latency observed in some routes.

What we’re doing next:
- Final postmortem with timeline, causal chain, and long-term remediation will be delivered by 2025-11-21 EOD.
- Engineering remediation will include a stricter rollout rule validation and an additional preflight check for KV snapshot alignment before toggle flips.
- We’ll provide packet/trace bundles and a redacted log set suitable for your audit team.

Attachments: interim_rca_20251120.pdf

I’ll set up a brief follow-up call if you’d like to review the final postmortem live — propose 11/24 or 11/25, or we can adjust to your calendar.

Apologies again for the disruption. We take availability seriously and will share corrective controls we’re adding across private deployments.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Redwood Inference

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Procurement Team <procurement@nimbushealth.com>
Date: 2025-11-21T16:05:00-08:00
Subject: FINAL Postmortem: REL-2921 — Nimbus private VPC control-plane interruption (2025-11-18)

Alex and Nimbus team — attaching the full postmortem and remediation plan. Key items below; please see the attached PDF for the complete timeline, logs, and remediation tickets.

Root cause (summary):
- A rollout rule mismatch caused a feature toggle (fast-fail on stale KV entries) to be enabled on a small subset (~12%) of private control-plane nodes serving Nimbus Health. The toggle’s fast-fail path assumes KV snapshot alignment; when mismatched it triggered transient request failures and retries that amplified latency.
- The mismatch stemmed from a deployment orchestration change that introduced asynchronous config propagation to private control-plane nodes. A preflight that validated KV snapshot fingerprints was omitted from the rollout for private clusters.

Impact:
- Duration: 2025-11-18 08:30–11:20 PST (primary impact).
- Error rate increase: peak ~18% of requests observed returning 504s.
- Customers affected: Nimbus Health (private VPC), other private tenants on the same control-plane partition were limited but not fully affected.

Remediation (deployed 2025-11-18 11:00–11:40):
- Immediate: rollback of the toggle to affected nodes, forced KV resync, and routing preference to stable leaders.
- Short-term: patch to orchestration to ensure consistent config application for private clusters; re-enabled synchronous snapshot verification.
- Long-term: additional preflight checks in our control-plane rollout pipeline (KV fingerprint match, routing-stability gate), improved canary window and automated rollback triggers for private deployments, and additional observability on snapshot divergence.

Follow-up actions for Nimbus (we will provide artifacts):
- Redacted trace bundle and packet-level evidence (suitable for your audit).
- A proposed customer credit for the impacted window (details enclosed in the PDF).
- Offer to join a postmortem review call next week to walk through the timeline.

Attachments: nimbus_postmortem_20251121.pdf

If you’d like an internal/executive summary tailored for procurement/compliance, I can produce that and copy your procurement mailbox.

Sincerely,
Evelyn Hart
Platform Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: nimbus_postmortem_20251121.pdf]
